posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
OK, so I am interested in the differences in alcohols and concentrations. So, what type of alcohol are people using and what differences do they find? In the US we have Isopropyl, Ethel and Methyl in a variety of concentrations. But when I read British papers they use a different denatured product. What are the differences?

Now, It is my understanding that if I dry a hologram (I have not tried) with submerging it from a water based bath into a heated 100% alcohol bath it will dry the outside layers more than the inner layers and make a broadband hologram. If I step it through a number of varying concentrations then I will end up with a narrow band hologram. Is this correct? 

Also, what is the max temperature I can safely use a alcohol bath?

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
> Now, It is my understanding that if I dry a hologram (I have not tried) with submerging it from a water based bath into a heated 100% alcohol bath it will dry the outside layers more than the inner layers and make a broadband hologram. If I step it through a number of varying concentrations then I will end up with a narrow band hologram. Is this correct?

Yes that is for the most part correct with DCG. The temperature change from one bath to another helps accentuate this. Cooler and temperatures closer together from one bath to the next helps with narrow band and warmer with temperatures with big steps from one to the next helps with broadband. Also short baths help broadband and longer baths in each alcohol help narrow band.

> Also, what is the max temperature I can safely use a alcohol bath?

I have never taken my alcohol to Dave's extreem. 120F (50c) is the hottest I usually use.
